questions.text: The Rajya Sabha is described as a 'permanent body' because ____.

options.option_text: its members serve for life, like the British House of Lords
it cannot be dissolved at any time, unlike the Lok Sabha
only the Supreme Court can dissolve it in a constitutional crisis
members are directly elected for non-renewable 10-year terms

questions.explanation: The Rajya Sabha is never dissolved as a whole — one-third of its members retire every two years, ensuring continuity. The Lok Sabha, by contrast, can be dissolved by the President on the Council of Ministers' advice (or automatically at the end of its 5-year term). Rajya Sabha members serve 6-year terms, not for life.

questions.text: A Money Bill under the Indian Constitution can be introduced only in the ____.

options.option_text: Rajya Sabha, after certification by the Vice-President
Lok Sabha; the Rajya Sabha can only suggest amendments
either House, at the Finance Minister's discretion
Joint Session of Parliament, on the President's recommendation

questions.explanation: Under Article 109, Money Bills can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha (with the President's prior recommendation). The Rajya Sabha may suggest amendments within 14 days, but the Lok Sabha is free to accept or reject them — the Rajya Sabha cannot amend or reject a Money Bill. The Speaker of Lok Sabha certifies whether a bill is a Money Bill.

questions.text: The maximum strength of the Rajya Sabha, as provided under Article 80, is ____.

options.option_text: 238 elected by State/UT legislatures + 12 nominated = 250 total
543 elected + 2 nominated by the President = 545 total
250 elected from States + 12 nominated by PM = 262 total
200 elected from States + 50 nominated by President = 250 total

questions.explanation: Article 80 fixes the Rajya Sabha maximum at 250: up to 238 elected representatives of States and UTs + 12 nominated by the President for distinguished service in literature, science, art, or social service. The current operational strength is 245. Option B describes the Lok Sabha (543 + 2 Anglo-Indian, now discontinued by 104th Amendment).

questions.text: A Joint Sitting of both Houses of Parliament (Article 108) is presided over by the ____.

options.option_text: President of India, as the constitutional head of Parliament
Vice-President of India, as ex-officio Chairman of Rajya Sabha
Speaker of the Lok Sabha, or Deputy Speaker in their absence
Chief Justice of India, as the constitutional arbiter

questions.explanation: Joint sittings are convened by the President to resolve deadlocks on ordinary bills, but presided over by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha (or Deputy Speaker if Speaker is absent; the Deputy Chairman of Rajya Sabha presides only if both are absent). Joint sittings have been held three times: Dowry Prohibition Bill (1961), Banking Service Commission Repeal (1978), POTA (2002).

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT an exclusive power of the Lok Sabha?

options.option_text: Passing a No-Confidence Motion to remove the Council of Ministers
Originating and passing all categories of Money Bills
Removing the Vice-President from office by a resolution
Granting or withholding supply (Union Budget approval)

questions.explanation: The Vice-President is removed under Article 67 by a resolution of the Rajya Sabha (passed by a majority) agreed to by the Lok Sabha — it originates in the Rajya Sabha, not an exclusive Lok Sabha power. No-Confidence Motions, originating Money Bills, and granting supply are exclusively Lok Sabha prerogatives. Compare: the President is removed by either House initiating impeachment.

options.option_text: MPs from all civil and criminal laws throughout their full parliamentary term in office
legislators' freedom of speech and votes within Parliament from external court proceedings
Parliament's right to override Supreme Court judgments on constitutional matters
Parliamentary debates and committee reports from all press and media reporting

questions.explanation: Parliamentary privilege guarantees that speeches, votes, and actions inside Parliament cannot be made the subject of court proceedings, ensuring free and frank debate. However, it does NOT grant immunity from criminal law generally (arrest for bribery is possible), does not override the judiciary, and press reporting of Parliamentary proceedings is generally permitted (subject to official secrets).

questions.text: Under Article 368, which type of constitutional amendment requires BOTH a special majority in Parliament AND ratification by at least half the State Legislatures?

options.option_text: Adding a new Fundamental Duty under Article 51A Part IV-A
Changing the name of a State under Article 3 procedures
Amending provisions for the election of the President (Articles 54–55)
Adding or removing a subject from the Concurrent List (List III)

questions.explanation: The Article 368 proviso lists federal provisions requiring state ratification: Articles 54/55 (President's election), 73/162 (executive power), federal judiciary articles, Seventh Schedule, representation of States in Parliament, and Article 368 itself. Fundamental Duties (Article 51A) and Concurrent List changes require only a special majority. Changing a State's name (Article 3) requires only a simple parliamentary majority.
